question: X5: two defects in the Overleaf sync script: push deadlocks after a real pull, and map.json is advanced before a push lands. Fix them?

solvers.answer: D-a: after any real pull of main2.tex, push deadlocks; fix with a pull watermark. D-b: map.json advances before the push lands; write it only after the push succeeds.

refutation.note: Both confirmed in overleaf_git.example.sh (the live copy differs only in the token line), with two related defects found: push-all stops the review layers under set -e, and the map is also written before --check runs. Neither has fired, since no collaborator has edited main2.tex.

final_answer: X5a: record a watermark at pull time (Overleaf commit SHA and the text consumed); push accepts Overleaf content equal to the last flatten or the last pulled text. X5b: write the map to a temporary path and move it into place only after the push succeeds; on rejection, reset the clone to origin and report. Automatic pull-and-retry waits for X7.
answer_short: The sync script records what each pull took in, so a push no longer refuses forever, and map.json is written only after a push lands.

actions.detail: Pull watermark; map written after the push lands; reset on rejection. Pending: a sync-code session; not yet applied.

consequences: Sync code only; needed before coauthors' edits can flow back (A5).
default: Applied in the next sync-code session.
